1. Let $X$ be a random variable that is normally distributed with mean 15 and variance 3. Let a sample be independently taken from this population with $n=20$. 

    a. Identify the sampling distribution of $\bar{X}$.
    b. What is the probability of $\bar{X}$ being within $2\sigma_{\bar{X}}$ of $\mu$? (i.e, $P(15-2\sigma_{\bar{X}} \leq \bar{X} \leq 15+2\sigma_{\bar{X}})$)
    c. A sample was taken from this population and found to have $\bar{X}=16.1$ and $s=1.5$. Compute $z$ and $t$.
    d. From your values computed in (c), compute $P(Z>z)$ and $P(T>t)$.


2. Suppose that $X_1,X_2,X_3$ come from a distribution with mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$, and are independent. Let $\hat{\theta}_1=\frac{X_1+X_2+X_3}{3}$ and $\hat{\theta}_2=\frac{X_1+2X_2+X_3}{4}$.

    a. Determine if $\hat{\theta}_1$ and $\hat{\theta}_2$ are unbiased estimators for $\mu$. 
    b. Compute $V(\hat{\theta}_1)$ and $V(\hat{\theta}_2)$, and identify which of the two estimators is more efficient.

3. Two independent random samples, each containing ten observations, were collected from normally distributed populations. Using R, manually compute the two-sided 95% confidence intervals for $\mu_1-\mu_2$ when (a) variances are equal, and (b) variances are unequal. For each interval, write a sentence to interpret the interval. Do not use the `t.test()` function (we will talk about this function later). Hint: many values need to be recalculated; save these into new objects to reuse.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
set.seed(380)
x1 <- round(rnorm(10, mean=10, sd=2),1)
x2 <- round(rnorm(10, mean=10, sd=2),1)
dput(x1)
dput(x2)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
x1 <- c(10.5, 10, 8.7, 14.2, 7.8, 6.1, 8.5, 11, 8.9, 10.7)
x2 <- c(10.5, 11, 8.1, 8.9, 10.1, 7.1, 11.3, 8.7, 11.6, 9.2)
```
